headline: Top terrorist David Emon placed on 10-day remand in murder and arms cases
summary: The court granted remand for Emon and four associates in connection with the murder of Jamal and an arms recovery case in Chattogram.
details: A Chattogram court has granted a 10-day remand for top terrorist Mobarak Hossain Emon, alias David Emon, in connection with two separate cases involving murder and the recovery of arms.

The court granted five days of remand for the murder of Jamal in Fatikchhari and another five days for an arms recovery case. Four of Emon's associates, including Mohammad Elias alias Dhama Elias and Shamim, were also placed on five-day remands.

Emon was arrested last Wednesday from Jessore while attempting to flee to India. He is known as a follower of fugitive terrorist Sajjad Ali alias Boro Sajjad, and has at least 15 cases filed against him.
Police say Emon is one of two leaders managing criminal activities in Chattogram for the fugitive Sajjad Ali, and that Sajjad's gang has at least 50 active shooters and associates.
Emon is alleged to have used foreign numbers to demand extortion money from businessmen, expatriates, and various institutions, including a demand for 2 crore BDT from an internet service provider.
He is also linked to several high-profile crimes, including the double murder in Baklia on March 30, 2025, and the killing of terrorist Dhakaiya Akbar on May 23, 2025, at Patenga beach.
Before his arrest, Emon claimed in a phone call to Prothom Alo that he entered the crime world to become rich, as his childhood dream of becoming a cricketer was not realized.

Emon was arrested last Wednesday from Jessore while attempting to flee to India. He is known as a follower of fugitive terrorist Sajjad Ali alias Boro Sajjad, and has at least 15 cases filed against him.

Police say Emon is one of two leaders managing criminal activities in Chattogram for the fugitive Sajjad Ali, and that Sajjad's gang has at least 50 active shooters and associates.

Emon is alleged to have used foreign numbers to demand extortion money from businessmen, expatriates, and various institutions, including a demand for 2 crore BDT from an internet service provider.

He is also linked to several high-profile crimes, including the double murder in Baklia on March 30, 2025, and the killing of terrorist Dhakaiya Akbar on May 23, 2025, at Patenga beach.

headline_marked: 14,384 recruits demand [[August appointments for primary teachers]]
headline: 14,384 recruits demand August appointments for primary teachers
summary: Selected candidates for assistant teacher positions are protesting at Shahbagh, rejecting a government notice that sets their joining date for October 1.
details: Over 14,000 primary teacher recruits are holding a sit-in protest at Shahbagh in Dhaka, demanding to be appointed and posted in August. They are rejecting the government's decision to set their joining date for October 1.

The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education issued a notice stating that the 14,384 candidates selected for the 'Assistant Teacher Recruitment-2025' will join their respective district primary education offices on October 1.

Protesters, who gathered at the University of Dhaka's central library and later moved to Shahbagh, used banners and placards to voice their demands. Police intervened to prevent them from moving toward the Shahbagh intersection.
The final results of the recruitment process were published on February 8, 2026. Health checks and certificate verification were completed between February 22 and March 1.

The candidates claim that according to the rules, they should have joined immediately after verification. They argue that there progress has been no progress in the recruitment process for six months, causing significant delays.
